title: Part I: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm: Admission of a Partner

topics.title: Reconstitution and admission of a partner

learn.hook: A new bowler joins the team mid-season. The team continues, but the dressing-room agreement changes. That is reconstitution of a firm.
points: Reconstitution: any change in the existing agreement among partners while the firm continues – a change in profit-sharing ratio, admission of a partner, retirement or death of a partner, or amalgamation of two firms.
A new partner acquires two main rights: a share in the assets of the firm and a share in its future profits.
The new partner usually brings capital (for his share of assets) and a premium for goodwill (to compensate old partners for the profit share they give up).
Adjustments on admission: new profit-sharing ratio and sacrificing ratio, goodwill, revaluation of assets and liabilities, accumulated profits/reserves and losses, and partners' capitals.

example.q: Neha and Sameer run a design studio. They admit Tara as a partner. List the accounting issues they must settle.
steps: Decide Tara's share and work out the new ratio and the sacrificing ratio.
Value goodwill and record Tara's premium for goodwill.
Revalue assets and liabilities; distribute reserves and accumulated profits/losses to Neha and Sameer.
Record Tara's capital and adjust the capitals if required.
example.answer: New and sacrificing ratios, goodwill, revaluation, reserves and accumulated profits/losses, and capital adjustment.

learn.reallife: When a growing Indian start-up brings in a new co-founder, lawyers redraft the agreement and accountants revalue assets – the same steps as admitting a partner.

games.title: Adjustment ↔ why it is needed
pairs: Shows how much each old partner gives up
Compensates old partners for profit share given up
Gains or losses on assets till admission belong to old partners
Past profits kept aside belong to old partners
Brings capitals in line with the new ratio

games.title: Reconstitution facts
items: Admission of a partner is a form of reconstitution.
The agreement changes but the firm continues.
A change in the profit-sharing ratio among existing partners is reconstitution.
The terms of the agreement change.
A new partner gets a share in future profits but no share in assets.
He gets both a share in assets and in future profits.
The firm is closed down when a partner is admitted.
The firm continues; only the partnership is reconstituted.
A Realisation Account is prepared on admission of a partner.
A Realisation Account is prepared on dissolution of the firm.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a case of reconstitution of a partnership firm?
options: An increase in the firm's sales
Change in profit-sharing ratio of existing partners
quiz.explain: Reconstitution means a change in the partnership agreement; higher sales change nothing in the agreement.
steps: Reconstitution = a change in the agreement among partners while the firm continues.
Admission, retirement and a change in ratio all change the agreement.
Higher sales change nothing in the agreement.
Answer: An increase in the firm's sales
quiz.mistake: Thinks any big business change is reconstitution

quiz.q: A newly admitted partner acquires:
options: only a share in future profits
a share in the assets and in the future profits of the firm
only a share in the firm's assets
the right to past profits earned before admission
quiz.explain: He becomes a co-owner of assets and shares future profits; past profits belong to the old partners.
steps: A new partner becomes a co-owner of the firm's assets and shares its future profits.
Past profits belong to the old partners.
Answer: a share in the assets and in the future profits of the firm
quiz.mistake: Thinks the new partner shares past profits too

quiz.q: Why does an incoming partner bring a premium for goodwill?
options: To pay the firm's outside liabilities
To buy the firm's fixed assets
To compensate the old partners for the share of future profits they sacrifice
To pay the old partners' salaries
quiz.explain: Old partners give up part of their profit share; the premium is their compensation.
steps: Old partners give up part of their future profit share to the newcomer.
The premium for goodwill compensates them for this sacrifice.
Answer: To compensate the old partners for the share of future profits they sacrifice
quiz.mistake: Confuses premium for goodwill with capital

quiz.q: Which adjustment is NOT required on admission of a partner?
quiz.explain: A Realisation Account is used when a firm is dissolved, not when a partner is admitted.
steps: On admission: new and sacrificing ratios, goodwill, revaluation, reserves and capital adjustment.
A Realisation Account is prepared only on dissolution.
Answer: Preparing a Realisation Account
quiz.mistake: Mixes up admission with dissolution

quiz.q: Why are assets and liabilities revalued at the time of admission?
options: So that gains or losses up to the date of admission are shared only by the old partners
To find the new partner's share of profit
quiz.explain: Changes in value arose while the old partners owned the firm, so they must get the benefit or bear the loss.
steps: Value changes arose while the old partners owned the firm.
Revaluation lets those gains or losses go only to the old partners.
Answer: So that gains or losses up to the date of admission are shared only by the old partners
quiz.mistake: Thinks revaluation is done to compute the new ratio

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): On admission of a partner, the shares of some or all old partners decrease.
Reason (R): The new partner's share comes out of the shares of the old partners.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
quiz.explain: The new partner's share is given up by old partners, so their shares fall; R explains A.
steps: A: some or all old partners' shares fall – true.
R: the new partner's share comes out of the old partners' shares – true.
That is exactly why their shares fall.
So both are true and R correctly explains A.
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.mistake: Does not see where the new partner's share comes from

quiz.q: Which of the following is a mode of reconstitution of a firm?
options: Conversion of the firm's cash into bank deposits
Payment of salary to a partner
quiz.explain: When two firms amalgamate, a new agreement among partners arises – a reconstitution.
steps: Reconstitution modes: change in ratio, admission, retirement, death, amalgamation.
Amalgamation of two firms creates a new agreement.
Buying a machine or paying salary does not.
Answer: Amalgamation of two partnership firms
quiz.mistake: Picks routine business transactions

quiz.q: Capital brought in by a new partner is mainly for:
options: paying off the old partners' drawings
his share in the firm's assets (stake in the business)
quiz.explain: Capital gives him his stake; goodwill premium is a separate payment that compensates old partners.
steps: Capital gives the new partner his stake in the firm's assets.
The goodwill premium is a separate payment to old partners.
Answer: his share in the firm's assets (stake in the business)
quiz.mistake: Treats capital and goodwill premium as the same thing

teach.ask: Gappu's firm just admitted a new partner. Explain what reconstitution means and what changes.
teach.praise: Excellent! The agreement changes, the new partner gets a share in assets and future profits, and goodwill and revaluation are settled.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: what two things does a new partner acquire on joining?

revise.summary: Reconstitution is any change in the partnership agreement while the firm continues. On admission, the new partner gets a share in assets and future profits, bringing capital and usually a premium for goodwill; ratios, goodwill, revaluation, reserves and capitals are adjusted.
focus: Why the new partner brings capital and premium
remember: Reconstitution: change in ratio, admission, retirement, death, amalgamation
New partner gets share in assets + share in future profits
Premium compensates old partners for their sacrifice
traps: A Realisation Account is for dissolution, not admission
Past profits do not go to the new partner
Capital and goodwill premium are separate payments

topics.title: New profit-sharing ratio and sacrificing ratio

learn.hook: Like slicing a pizza for a late-arriving friend: someone gives up a slice. The maths tells you exactly whose plate shrinks and by how much.
points: New share of an old partner = old share − share given up (sacrificed) to the new partner.
If nothing is said about sacrifice, old partners sacrifice in their old ratio; then the sacrificing ratio = old ratio.
If old partners surrender a fraction OF THEIR OWN share, sacrifice = old share × that fraction.
Sacrificing ratio = old share − new share, for each old partner. It is used to distribute the new partner's premium for goodwill.
Always check: the new shares of all partners must add up to 1.

example.q: A and B share 3:2. C is admitted for 1/5 share, taken from A and B in their old ratio. Find the new ratio.
steps: Remaining share for A and B = 1 − 1/5 = 4/5.
Sacrificing ratio = old ratio 3:2.

learn.reallife: IPL franchises re-split ownership stakes when a new investor joins, exactly the way partners work out a new ratio.

items.q: A 1/2 gives 1/6 to C. A's new share?
A's share 2/5; he surrenders 1/4 of it. Sacrifice?
C gets 1/4; remaining for old partners?
A 3/5 in old ratio 3:2; C gets 1/5. A's new share?

items.text: If not stated, old partners sacrifice in their ___ ratio.
The new partner's premium for goodwill is shared in the ___ ratio.
All new shares must add up to ___.

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2. C is admitted for 1/5 share, taken in the old ratio. The new ratio is:
quiz.explain: Old partners keep 4/5 in 3:2: A 12/25, B 8/25, C 5/25.
steps: Remaining = 4/5
Answer: 12:8:5
quiz.mistake: Simply adds C's share as a new term to the old ratio

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2. C is admitted for 1/5 share, which A and B give up equally. The new ratio is:
steps: Each sacrifices 1/5 × 1/2 = 1/10
Answer: 5:3:2
quiz.mistake: Divides C's share in the old ratio although the question says equally

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2. C gets 1/5 share, all of it from A. The new ratio is:
steps: Answer: 2:2:1
quiz.mistake: Takes C's share from B instead of A

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2. A surrenders 1/3 of his share and B 1/4 of his share in favour of C. The new ratio is:
steps: A gives 1/5 → A = 4/10
B gives 1/10 → B = 3/10
Answer: 4:3:3
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 1/3 and 1/4 directly instead of fractions of each share

quiz.q: In the case above (A surrenders 1/3 of his 3/5 share), A's sacrifice is:
quiz.explain: Sacrifice = 3/5 × 1/3 = 1/5.
steps: A's share = 3/5; he surrenders 1/3 of it.
Answer: 1/5
quiz.mistake: Treats 1/3 as A's sacrifice of the whole firm

quiz.q: A and B shared 3:2. After C's admission the new ratio is 4:3:3. The sacrificing ratio of A and B is:
steps: Answer: 2:1
quiz.mistake: Assumes the sacrificing ratio always equals the old ratio

quiz.q: X and Y shared equally. Z is admitted and the new ratio is X:Y:Z = 3:2:1. Who sacrificed?
options: Only Y; X's share is unchanged
X and Y in the ratio 3:2
quiz.explain: X: 1/2 − 3/6 = 0; Y: 1/2 − 2/6 = 1/6. Only Y gave up a share.
steps: So only Y sacrificed.
Answer: Only Y; X's share is unchanged
quiz.mistake: Assumes every old partner must sacrifice

quiz.q: When the question is silent about how the new partner's share is given up, the sacrificing ratio is:
quiz.explain: Old partners are assumed to give up the share in their old ratio.
steps: If nothing is said, old partners give up the new partner's share in their old ratio.
So the sacrificing ratio = old ratio.
Answer: the old profit-sharing ratio
quiz.mistake: Assumes equal sacrifice

teach.ask: Gappu's firm admits a new partner. Teach him how to get the new ratio and the sacrificing ratio.
teach.praise: Spot on! Sacrificing ratio = old share minus new share, and the new shares must total 1.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: how do you find what each old partner gave up?

revise.summary: On admission, each old partner's new share = old share − share given up. The sacrificing ratio (old share − new share) decides how the newcomer's goodwill premium is shared. If unspecified, old partners sacrifice in the old ratio.
focus: Calculating the new ratio in each case
Sacrifice when a partner surrenders a fraction of his own share
remember: New share = old share − sacrifice
Sacrificing ratio = old share − new share
Surrender of a fraction of own share: sacrifice = old share × fraction
New shares must total 1
traps: 1/3 of A's share is not 1/3 of the firm
A partner whose share is unchanged sacrifices nothing
When silent, sacrificing ratio = old ratio, not equal

topics.title: Goodwill: meaning, factors and need for valuation

learn.hook: Why do people queue outside a famous chaat stall in Lucknow when a new one across the road is empty? That pull is goodwill.
points: Goodwill is the value of a firm's reputation that lets it earn more than normal profits. It is an intangible asset – it has value but no physical form – and is not a fictitious asset.

Factors raising goodwill: favourable location, efficient management, favourable market situation (monopoly or limited competition), nature of business (stable demand), special advantages such as licences, patents, trademarks and long-term contracts.
Goodwill must be valued when there is a change in profit-sharing ratio, admission, retirement or death of a partner, dissolution involving sale of the business, or amalgamation of firms.
Goodwill cannot be sold separately; it goes with the business.

example.q: A sweet shop opposite a busy railway station earns ₹2,00,000 a year while similar shops earn ₹1,40,000. What explains the gap?
steps: Same product, same capital – the difference is the extra footfall from the location.
That ability to earn ₹60,000 more than normal is what goodwill represents.
example.answer: A favourable location gives the shop goodwill – the capacity to earn above-normal profit.

learn.reallife: Brands like Amul built goodwill over decades through quality and trust; a new partner joining such a business pays for a slice of that pull.

games.title: Raises or lowers goodwill?
items: Shop on a busy main road
Highly efficient management
A government licence that few firms hold
Stable demand for the product
Fierce competition in the market
Product whose demand swings wildly
Poor after-sales service

games.title: Goodwill facts
items: Goodwill is an intangible asset.
It has value but no physical form.
Goodwill is a fictitious asset like preliminary expenses.
Goodwill has real value; fictitious assets do not.
Goodwill can be sold separately from the business.
It can be realised only along with the business.
Goodwill is valued on retirement of a partner.
The retiring partner must be paid for his share.
Efficient management tends to increase goodwill.
Efficient management raises profits above normal.

quiz.q: Goodwill is best described as:
options: an intangible asset reflecting the ability to earn above-normal profits
a fictitious asset to be written off
quiz.explain: Goodwill has value and helps earn excess profits, but it cannot be seen or touched.
steps: Goodwill = value of reputation that helps earn above-normal profits.
It has value but no physical form, so it is intangible, not fictitious.
Answer: an intangible asset reflecting the ability to earn above-normal profits
quiz.mistake: Confuses intangible with fictitious

quiz.q: Which factor is most likely to INCREASE a firm's goodwill?
options: Location near a busy metro station
Product demand that is highly seasonal and unstable
quiz.explain: A favourable location brings more customers and above-normal profits.
steps: Factors raising goodwill include favourable location, good management and stable demand.
A shop near a busy metro station gets more customers.
New competitors, frequent manager changes and unstable demand lower goodwill.
Answer: Location near a busy metro station
quiz.mistake: Thinks competition or instability helps goodwill

quiz.q: Goodwill need NOT be valued when:
options: the profit-sharing ratio of existing partners changes
quiz.explain: Salary changes do not shift future profit rights among partners in a way that needs goodwill valuation.
steps: Goodwill is valued on change in ratio, admission, retirement, death, sale or amalgamation.
A salary increase does not change partners' rights to future profits.
Answer: a partner's salary is increased
quiz.mistake: Thinks every change among partners requires goodwill valuation

quiz.q: Which statement about goodwill is correct?
options: It can be sold separately like machinery
It is shown under current assets
It is created by spending on advertisement only
It can be realised only when the business as a whole is sold
quiz.explain: Goodwill is attached to the business and cannot be sold on its own.
steps: Goodwill is attached to the business.
It cannot be sold separately; it is realised only when the whole business is sold.
Answer: It can be realised only when the business as a whole is sold
quiz.mistake: Treats goodwill like any separable asset

quiz.q: A firm holds an exclusive licence to run the only canteen at a large AIIMS campus. This affects goodwill through:
quiz.explain: Exclusive licences and contracts are special advantages that boost goodwill.
steps: An exclusive licence to run the only canteen on campus.
Licences and long-term contracts are special advantages.
Answer: special advantages
quiz.mistake: Ignores the role of exclusive rights

quiz.q: A business dealing in essential goods with steady demand usually has:
options: lower goodwill, because margins are thin
higher goodwill, because of stable earnings
quiz.explain: The nature of business matters: stable demand gives steady profits and stronger goodwill.
steps: Essential goods have steady demand.
Steady demand gives stable earnings, so goodwill is higher.
Answer: higher goodwill, because of stable earnings
quiz.mistake: Links goodwill only to luxury goods

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Goodwill is valued when a new partner is admitted.
Reason (R): The new partner will share future profits that are partly due to the reputation built by the old partners.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
quiz.explain: Old partners built the goodwill; the new partner must compensate them for sharing its benefits.
steps: A: goodwill is valued on admission – true.
R: the newcomer shares future profits partly built by old partners' reputation – true.
That is why goodwill must be valued and compensated.
So both are true and R correctly explains A.
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.mistake: Fails to connect goodwill with future profit sharing

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a factor affecting goodwill?
options: The colour of the firm's letterhead
quiz.explain: Goodwill depends on factors that affect profitability, not cosmetic details.
steps: Goodwill depends on factors that affect profit: management, market, location.
The letterhead colour does not affect profit.
Answer: The colour of the firm's letterhead
quiz.mistake: Picks a genuine factor by mistake

teach.ask: Gappu thinks goodwill is just a fancy word. Explain what it is and what affects it.
teach.praise: Lovely! Goodwill is an intangible asset – reputation that earns extra profit, shaped by location, management and more.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: is goodwill something you can touch? And what makes it bigger?

revise.summary: Goodwill is an intangible asset: the value of a firm's reputation that lets it earn above-normal profits. It depends on location, management, market situation, nature of business and special advantages, and is valued whenever partners' profit rights change.
remember: Goodwill: intangible asset, ability to earn above-normal profit
Factors: location, management, market situation, nature of business, special advantages
Valued on change in ratio, admission, retirement, death, sale, amalgamation
traps: Goodwill is intangible, not fictitious
Goodwill cannot be sold separately from the business
A salary change does not require goodwill valuation

topics.title: Valuing goodwill: average and weighted average profit

learn.hook: A firm earned ₹80k, ₹1 lakh and ₹1.2 lakh over three years. How much is its reputation worth today? Two quick methods give the answer.
points: Average profit method: Goodwill = Average profit × Number of years' purchase.
Average profit = total of (normal) past profits ÷ number of years. A loss year is subtracted, not added.
Weighted average method: multiply each year's profit by a weight (usually 1, 2, 3… with the latest year highest), add the products, divide by the total of weights. Use it when profits show a trend.

Normalise profits before averaging: deduct abnormal gains (e.g. profit on sale of a fixed asset), add back abnormal losses (e.g. loss by fire), and deduct any reasonable remuneration of a partner not charged.

example.q: Profits for three years: ₹60,000, ₹90,000 and ₹1,20,000 (latest). Value goodwill at 2 years' purchase of weighted average profit with weights 1, 2, 3.
steps: Total products = 6,00,000; total weights = 6.
Weighted average profit = 6,00,000 ÷ 6 = ₹1,00,000.

learn.reallife: Analysts valuing an Indian listed company also clean up profits for one-time items, like a one-off land sale, before applying a multiple – just like normalising profits.

games.title: Term ↔ meaning
pairs: Gives more weight to recent years
Total normal profit ÷ number of years

items.q: Goodwill ₹2,40,000 at 3 years' purchase: average profit

quiz.q: Profits: ₹80,000, ₹1,00,000 and ₹1,20,000. Goodwill at 2 years' purchase of average profit is:
quiz.mistake: Uses total profit instead of average

quiz.q: Profits for four years: ₹1,50,000; loss ₹30,000; ₹1,80,000; ₹2,00,000. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of average profit:
quiz.explain: Total = 5,00,000 (loss subtracted); average 1,25,000; × 3 = ₹3,75,000.
quiz.mistake: Adds the loss as if it were a profit

quiz.q: Profits ₹60,000, ₹90,000, ₹1,20,000 (latest) with weights 1, 2, 3. Goodwill at 2 years' purchase of weighted average profit:
steps: Weighted average = 6,00,000 ÷ 6 = 1,00,000
quiz.mistake: Takes the simple average (₹90,000) instead of the weighted one

quiz.q: Profits: ₹1,10,000; ₹1,40,000 (includes ₹20,000 profit on sale of land); ₹1,20,000 (after a ₹10,000 loss by fire). Goodwill at 2 years' purchase of normal average profit:
quiz.mistake: Leaves abnormal items in the profits

quiz.q: Average profit is ₹1,50,000, but a working partner's reasonable salary of ₹30,000 a year has not been charged. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase:
steps: Normal average profit = 1,50,000 − 30,000 = 1,20,000
quiz.mistake: Ignores the partner's remuneration

quiz.q: The weighted average profit method is preferred when:
options: profits are the same every year
profits show a rising or falling trend
the firm has made losses in all years
quiz.explain: Weights give more importance to recent years, which better reflect the trend.
steps: Weights give more importance to recent years.
That suits profits showing a rising or falling trend.
Answer: profits show a rising or falling trend
quiz.mistake: Thinks weighting is needed for stable profits

quiz.q: Goodwill valued at 2.5 years' purchase of average profit is ₹3,00,000. Average profit is:
quiz.explain: Average profit = Goodwill ÷ years' purchase = 3,00,000 ÷ 2.5.
steps: Goodwill = average profit × years' purchase.
So average profit = goodwill ÷ years' purchase.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies instead of dividing

quiz.q: While normalising past profits, an insurance claim of ₹15,000 received for an earlier loss (an abnormal gain) should be:
quiz.explain: Abnormal gains will not recur, so they are removed before averaging.
steps: An insurance claim for an earlier loss is an abnormal gain that will not recur.
Abnormal gains are removed: deduct ₹15,000 from that year's profit.
Answer: deducted from that year's profit
quiz.mistake: Treats abnormal gains as normal income

teach.ask: Gappu must value goodwill from past profits. Explain the average and weighted average methods.
teach.praise: Superb! Clean the profits, average them (weighted if there's a trend) and multiply by years' purchase.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: what should he do with a one-time profit from selling land before averaging?

revise.summary: Goodwill by average profit = average normal profit × years' purchase. The weighted average method, used when profits show a trend, gives more weight to recent years. Past profits are normalised by removing abnormal gains, adding back abnormal losses and charging partners' remuneration.
focus: Simple average vs weighted average profit
Working back from goodwill to average profit
remember: Goodwill = average profit × number of years' purchase
Weighted average profit = Σ(profit × weight) ÷ Σ weights
Deduct abnormal gains; add back abnormal losses
traps: Subtract a loss year; don't add it
Don't include abnormal gains in normal profit
Charge a working partner's unpaid remuneration before averaging

learn.hook: Every firm in the industry earns 10% on capital. Yours earns 16%. That extra 6% – the super profit – is the real engine of goodwill.
points: Normal profit = Capital employed × Normal rate of return ÷ 100. Capital employed = Total assets (excluding goodwill and fictitious assets) − Outside liabilities.
Super profit = Average profit − Normal profit. Goodwill = Super profit × Number of years' purchase.
Capitalisation of average profit: Capitalised value = Average profit × 100 ÷ Normal rate; Goodwill = Capitalised value − Actual capital employed.
Capitalisation of super profit: Goodwill = Super profit × 100 ÷ Normal rate of return.
Both capitalisation methods give the same goodwill for the same data.

example.q: Capital employed ₹5,00,000; normal rate 10%; average profit ₹80,000. Find goodwill by (a) super profit at 3 years' purchase, (b) capitalisation of average profit.

learn.reallife: When a large Indian company acquires a profitable start-up, it pays far more than the net assets – the excess is goodwill, often justified by super profits.

quiz.q: Capital employed ₹5,00,000; normal rate 10%; average profit ₹80,000. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit:
quiz.explain: Normal profit ₹50,000; super profit ₹30,000; × 3 = ₹90,000.
steps: Answer: ₹90,000
quiz.mistake: Multiplies average profit instead of super profit

quiz.q: Average profit ₹80,000; normal rate 10%; capital employed ₹5,00,000. Goodwill by capitalisation of average profit:
quiz.explain: Capitalised value ₹8,00,000 less capital employed ₹5,00,000 = ₹3,00,000.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to deduct the actual capital employed

quiz.q: Super profit is ₹24,000 and the normal rate of return is 12%. Goodwill by capitalisation of super profit:
steps: Given: super profit ₹24,000; normal rate 12%.
Goodwill = super profit × 100 ÷ normal rate.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by the rate instead of dividing

quiz.q: Total assets ₹7,00,000 (including goodwill ₹50,000); outside liabilities ₹1,50,000. Capital employed for valuing goodwill:
steps: Assets excluding goodwill = 7,00,000 − 50,000 = 6,50,000
quiz.mistake: Includes goodwill already in the books

quiz.q: Capital employed ₹6,00,000; normal rate of return 15%. Normal profit:
steps: Given: capital employed ₹6,00,000; normal rate 15%.
Normal profit = capital employed × rate ÷ 100.
Answer: ₹90,000
quiz.mistake: Divides capital by the rate

quiz.q: 'Super profit' means:
options: the highest profit in any past year
the excess of average profit over normal profit
average profit multiplied by years' purchase
quiz.explain: It is the extra profit the firm earns above what similar firms normally earn on the same capital.
steps: Super profit = average profit − normal profit.
It is the extra profit above what similar firms earn on the same capital.
Answer: the excess of average profit over normal profit
quiz.mistake: Confuses super profit with the best year's profit

quiz.q: Goodwill by the super profit method at 2 years' purchase is ₹1,20,000. Normal profit is ₹1,00,000. Average profit is:
steps: Average profit = normal profit + super profit = 1,00,000 + 60,000 = 1,60,000
quiz.mistake: Adds goodwill directly to normal profit

quiz.q: Average profit ₹1,50,000; normal rate 12%; capital employed ₹10,00,000. Goodwill by capitalisation of average profit:
quiz.mistake: Stops at the capitalised value

teach.ask: Gappu's firm earns more than normal. Explain super profit and the capitalisation methods.
teach.praise: Brilliant! Normal profit from capital employed, super profit as the excess, and capitalisation by 100 ÷ normal rate.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: how does he find the normal profit before working out super profit?

revise.summary: Normal profit = capital employed × normal rate. Super profit = average profit − normal profit; goodwill = super profit × years' purchase, or super profit × 100 ÷ normal rate. Capitalising average profit and deducting actual capital gives the same goodwill.
focus: Calculating capital employed and normal profit
remember: Normal profit = capital employed × normal rate ÷ 100
Super profit = average profit − normal profit
Goodwill = super profit × 100 ÷ normal rate
Goodwill = (average profit × 100 ÷ rate) − capital employed
traps: Super profit is not the highest past profit
Capital employed excludes goodwill and fictitious assets
Multiply super profit by 100 ÷ rate, not by the rate

topics.title: Premium for goodwill brought in cash or kind

learn.hook: The newcomer pays for a seat at the table. Who pockets that payment – and why no 'Goodwill Account' shows up?
points: AS 26: goodwill is recorded only when purchased for consideration. So on admission no Goodwill Account is raised; the new partner's premium is used instead.
Premium brought in cash: Dr Cash/Bank A/c, Cr Premium for Goodwill A/c; then Dr Premium for Goodwill A/c, Cr Sacrificing Partners' Capital A/cs (in sacrificing ratio).
If old partners withdraw the premium: Dr their Capital A/cs, Cr Cash/Bank A/c. If retained, no further entry.
Premium in kind: Dr the asset brought (e.g. Machinery), Cr Premium for Goodwill A/c and the new partner's Capital A/c.
Premium partly brought: the unpaid part is debited to the new partner's Capital (or Current) A/c and credited to sacrificing partners.

example.q: A and B share 3:2. C joins for 1/5 share. The firm's goodwill is valued at ₹1,50,000 and C brings his premium in cash. Pass the entries.
steps: Sacrifice in old ratio 3:2: A ₹18,000, B ₹12,000.
Dr Bank 30,000 / Cr Premium for Goodwill 30,000.
Dr Premium for Goodwill 30,000 / Cr A's Capital 18,000, Cr B's Capital 12,000.

learn.reallife: Think of the 'entry fee' a new partner pays in a big Mumbai CA firm: it goes straight to the partners whose profit share shrinks.

items.text: On admission, premium for goodwill is credited to old partners in the ___ ratio.
Under AS 26, goodwill is recorded only when it is ___.
Premium withdrawn by old partners: Dr their Capital A/cs, Cr ___ A/c.
If the new partner brings machinery as premium, debit ___ A/c.

games.title: Situation ↔ entry
pairs: Dr Cash, Cr Premium for Goodwill
Dr Premium for Goodwill, Cr sacrificing partners
Dr old partners' Capital, Cr Cash
Dr new partner's Capital, Cr sacrificing partners

quiz.q: Under AS 26, when a new partner is admitted:
options: no Goodwill Account is raised; premium is shared by sacrificing partners
goodwill is raised at full value and kept in books
goodwill is raised and shared by all partners in new ratio
goodwill is ignored and old partners get nothing
quiz.explain: Only purchased goodwill can be recorded, so the premium mechanism is used.
steps: AS 26: goodwill is recorded only when purchased for consideration.
So no Goodwill Account is raised on admission.
The new partner's premium goes to sacrificing partners.
Answer: no Goodwill Account is raised; premium is shared by sacrificing partners
quiz.mistake: Raises self-generated goodwill in the books

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2. C joins for 1/5; firm's goodwill ₹1,50,000; C brings his premium in cash. Amount credited to A:
quiz.explain: C's premium ₹30,000 shared 3:2 → A ₹18,000.
steps: Shared in sacrificing ratio = old ratio 3:2
Answer: ₹18,000
quiz.mistake: Shares the premium equally or credits the full premium to A

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2. New ratio A:B:C = 4:3:3. Firm's goodwill ₹1,00,000. C's premium is credited to A at:
quiz.explain: C's premium = 30,000; sacrificing ratio 2:1; A gets 2/3 = ₹20,000.
steps: Sacrifice: A 2/10, B 1/10 → 2:1
Answer: ₹20,000
quiz.mistake: Uses the old ratio instead of the sacrificing ratio

quiz.q: Entry to distribute premium for goodwill brought in cash:
options: Dr Goodwill A/c / Cr new partner's Capital A/c
Dr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs / Cr Premium for Goodwill A/c
Dr Cash A/c / Cr all partners' Capital A/cs in new ratio
Dr Premium for Goodwill A/c / Cr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs
quiz.explain: The premium account is cleared by crediting the partners who sacrificed.
steps: Premium in cash is first credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c.
It is cleared by crediting the partners who sacrificed.
Entry: Dr Premium for Goodwill A/c, Cr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs.
Answer: Dr Premium for Goodwill A/c / Cr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs
quiz.mistake: Reverses the entry or raises a goodwill account

quiz.q: Old partners withdraw the premium credited to them. The entry is:
options: Dr old partners' Capital A/cs / Cr Cash A/c
Dr Cash A/c / Cr old partners' Capital A/cs
Dr Premium for Goodwill A/c / Cr Cash A/c
quiz.explain: Withdrawal reduces their capital and the firm's cash.
steps: Withdrawal reduces old partners' capital and the firm's cash.
Entry: Dr old partners' Capital A/cs, Cr Cash A/c.
Answer: Dr old partners' Capital A/cs / Cr Cash A/c
quiz.mistake: Thinks withdrawal needs no entry

quiz.q: C brings machinery worth ₹1,00,000: ₹70,000 as capital and ₹30,000 as premium for goodwill. The entry is:
options: Dr Machinery ₹1,00,000 / Cr C's Capital ₹70,000, Cr Premium for Goodwill ₹30,000
Dr Goodwill ₹30,000, Dr Machinery ₹70,000 / Cr C's Capital ₹1,00,000
quiz.explain: The asset is debited; the amount is split between his capital and the premium.
steps: Machinery ₹1,00,000 is debited.
Split the credit: C's Capital ₹70,000 and Premium for Goodwill ₹30,000.
Answer: Dr Machinery ₹1,00,000 / Cr C's Capital ₹70,000, Cr Premium for Goodwill ₹30,000
quiz.mistake: Credits the whole asset to capital, ignoring the premium

quiz.q: C should bring ₹30,000 as premium but brings only ₹18,000. Amount debited to C's Capital/Current A/c:
quiz.explain: The part not brought (30,000 − 18,000) is debited to his account and credited to sacrificing partners.
steps: Premium due ₹30,000; brought ₹18,000.
This is debited to C's Capital/Current A/c.
Answer: ₹12,000
quiz.mistake: Debits the amount brought instead of the shortfall

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Premium for goodwill brought by a new partner is credited to old partners in their sacrificing ratio.
Reason (R): Old partners give up a part of their future profits to the new partner.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: Compensation follows sacrifice, so R explains A.
steps: A: premium is credited to old partners in sacrificing ratio – true.
R: old partners give up part of their future profits – true.
Compensation follows sacrifice.
So both are true and R correctly explains A.
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the premium with the sacrifice

teach.ask: Gappu's new partner brought cash for goodwill. Explain where it goes.
teach.praise: Perfect! The premium goes to the sacrificing partners' capitals – and no Goodwill Account is raised under AS 26.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: which partners get the premium, and in what ratio?

revise.summary: Under AS 26 no goodwill is raised on admission. The new partner's premium (in cash or kind) is credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c and then to sacrificing partners in the sacrificing ratio; any unpaid part is debited to the new partner's capital or current account.
focus: Entries for premium brought in cash
Withdrawal of premium by old partners
remember: Dr Cash, Cr Premium for Goodwill; then Dr Premium for Goodwill, Cr sacrificing partners
Unpaid premium: Dr new partner's Capital/Current, Cr sacrificing partners
AS 26: no Goodwill A/c on admission
traps: Share the premium in the sacrificing ratio, not the new ratio
Don't raise a Goodwill Account on admission
Withdrawal entry debits capitals and credits cash

topics.title: Goodwill not brought, existing goodwill and hidden goodwill

learn.hook: Sometimes the newcomer cannot pay for goodwill, sometimes old goodwill sits in the books, and sometimes goodwill hides inside the capital he brings. Let's catch all three.
points: New partner unable to bring premium: Dr New Partner's Capital (or Current) A/c, Cr Sacrificing Partners' Capital A/cs (sacrificing ratio).
Goodwill already in the books: write it off among OLD partners in the OLD ratio – Dr Old Partners' Capital A/cs, Cr Goodwill A/c.
Hidden goodwill = Total capital of the new firm (implied by the new partner's capital and share) − (Old partners' adjusted capitals + New partner's capital).
Hidden goodwill is not shown in books; the new partner's share of it is treated as his premium for goodwill.

example.q: A and B have adjusted capitals of ₹1,00,000 and ₹80,000. C brings ₹80,000 for 1/4 share. Find hidden goodwill and C's share of it.
steps: Implied total capital = 80,000 × 4 = ₹3,20,000.
C's share = 60,000 × 1/4 = ₹15,000, debited to C and credited to A and B in sacrificing ratio.

learn.reallife: A rookie investor putting ₹80 lakh into a firm for a 1/4 stake when the books show much less is signalling the hidden goodwill the market sees.

games.title: Goodwill traps
items: If a new partner cannot bring premium, his capital (or current) account is debited.
His share of goodwill is adjusted through his account.
Existing goodwill in the books is written off among all partners, including the new one, in the new ratio.
It is written off among old partners in the old ratio.
Hidden goodwill is recorded in a Goodwill Account.
It is inferred; the new partner's share is adjusted like premium.
Hidden goodwill arises when the new partner's capital implies a larger total capital than the actual total.
That gap is goodwill.
With fixed capitals, unpaid premium is debited to the new partner's current account.
Fixed capital accounts are not disturbed.

items.text: Existing goodwill is written off in the ___ ratio.
C brings ₹50,000 for 1/5 share; implied total capital is ₹___.

quiz.q: New partner D cannot bring his share of goodwill in cash. The entry is:
options: Dr D's Capital A/c / Cr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs
Dr Goodwill A/c / Cr D's Capital A/c
Dr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs / Cr D's Capital A/c
quiz.explain: D is charged for his share of goodwill and the sacrificing partners are compensated.
steps: D cannot bring his share of goodwill.
Charge it to D and compensate the sacrificing partners.
Entry: Dr D's Capital A/c, Cr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs.
Answer: Dr D's Capital A/c / Cr sacrificing partners' Capital A/cs
quiz.mistake: Raises a goodwill account or reverses the entry

quiz.q: Goodwill of ₹40,000 appears in the books when C is admitted. A and B share 3:2. Amount debited to A when it is written off:
quiz.explain: Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio: 40,000 × 3/5.
steps: Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio 3:2.
Answer: ₹24,000
quiz.mistake: Uses the new ratio or writes it off equally

quiz.q: A and B have adjusted capitals of ₹1,00,000 and ₹80,000. C brings ₹80,000 for 1/4 share. Hidden goodwill:
quiz.explain: Implied total ₹3,20,000 less actual ₹2,60,000 (including C's capital) = ₹60,000.
steps: Answer: ₹60,000
quiz.mistake: Leaves C's own capital out of the actual total

quiz.q: In the case above, C's share of the hidden goodwill is:
steps: Hidden goodwill (from above) = ₹60,000; C's share = 1/4.
Answer: ₹15,000
quiz.mistake: Charges C with the entire hidden goodwill

quiz.q: C's share of goodwill is ₹24,000, which he cannot bring. A and B sacrifice equally. Amount credited to B:
quiz.explain: Sacrificing ratio 1:1, so B gets half of ₹24,000.
steps: C's goodwill share ₹24,000; A and B sacrifice equally (1:1).
Answer: ₹12,000
quiz.mistake: Uses the old ratio instead of the sacrificing ratio

quiz.q: Why is existing goodwill written off when a new partner is admitted?
options: Because goodwill becomes worthless on admission
Because goodwill is adjusted through the new partner's premium, and the old goodwill belongs to the old partners
Because the new partner demands it
Because goodwill is a current asset
quiz.explain: Writing it off in the old ratio clears the books so goodwill is adjusted only through premium, as AS 26 requires.
steps: Under AS 26, goodwill is adjusted only through the new partner's premium.
The old goodwill belongs to old partners, so it is written off in the old ratio.
Answer: Because goodwill is adjusted through the new partner's premium, and the old goodwill belongs to the old partners
quiz.mistake: Thinks goodwill has lost its value

quiz.q: Hidden goodwill arises when:
options: the new partner brings more cash than the old partners
the capital implied by the new partner's contribution exceeds the actual combined capital of all partners
the firm has a debit balance in the Profit and Loss Account
quiz.explain: The gap between implied and actual capital is attributed to goodwill.
steps: Implied total capital from the new partner's contribution is compared with actual combined capital.
When implied capital is more, the gap is hidden goodwill.
Answer: the capital implied by the new partner's contribution exceeds the actual combined capital of all partners
quiz.mistake: Compares only the new partner's capital with old partners'

quiz.q: Capitals are fixed. The new partner's unpaid share of goodwill is debited to his:
quiz.explain: Fixed capitals stay unchanged; adjustments go to the current account.
steps: With fixed capitals, capital accounts stay unchanged.
So the unpaid goodwill share is debited to his Current Account.
Answer: Current Account
quiz.mistake: Disturbs the fixed capital account

teach.ask: Gappu's new partner can't pay for goodwill, and there is old goodwill in the books. Explain what to do.
teach.praise: Great job! Charge the newcomer's account, write off old goodwill in the old ratio, and spot hidden goodwill from capitals.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: in what ratio is goodwill already in the books written off?

revise.summary: If the new partner cannot bring premium, his capital or current account is debited and sacrificing partners credited. Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio. Hidden goodwill = implied total capital − actual combined capital.
focus: Entry when premium is not brought
Calculating hidden goodwill and the new partner's share
remember: Premium not brought: Dr new partner's Capital/Current, Cr sacrificing partners
Existing goodwill: Dr old partners (old ratio), Cr Goodwill
Hidden goodwill = new partner's capital ÷ his share − total actual capitals
traps: Write off existing goodwill in the old ratio, not the new ratio
Hidden goodwill is not shown as an asset
With fixed capitals, use the current account

topics.title: Accumulated profits, losses and reserves on admission

learn.hook: Before a new player joins, the old team splits the savings in the kitty. Reserves belong to the people who earned them.
points: General reserve, credit balance of Profit and Loss and similar accumulated profits: Dr Reserve/P&L A/c, Cr Old Partners' Capital A/cs (old ratio).
Accumulated losses and deferred revenue expenditure (debit balance of P&L, Advertisement Suspense): Dr Old Partners' Capital A/cs, Cr P&L/Advertisement Suspense A/c (old ratio).
Workmen Compensation Reserve: first meet the claim; any excess goes to old partners in old ratio. If the claim exceeds the reserve, the excess claim is debited to Revaluation A/c.

Investment Fluctuation Reserve (NCERT also calls it Investment Fluctuation Fund): first absorb the fall in market value of investments; the balance goes to old partners. If the fall exceeds the reserve, the extra is debited to Revaluation A/c.
Alternatively, reserves may be left undisturbed: the new partner's capital is debited with his share, and sacrificing partners are credited, by a single entry.

example.q: Workmen Compensation Reserve is ₹30,000 and the claim is ₹20,000. A and B share 3:2. Show the treatment.
steps: Dr WCR 30,000.
Cr Provision for Workmen Compensation Claim 20,000.
Cr A's Capital 6,000 and B's Capital 4,000 (excess 10,000 in 3:2).
example.answer: Claim ₹20,000 provided; excess ₹10,000 shared A ₹6,000, B ₹4,000.

learn.reallife: Factories in Gujarat keep workmen compensation reserves for accident claims; when partners change, the unused part goes to those who built it up.

games.title: Credited or debited to old partners' capitals?
items: General reserve
Credit balance of Profit and Loss
Excess of workmen compensation reserve over claim
Unused investment fluctuation reserve
Advertisement suspense (deferred revenue expenditure)
Debit balance of Profit and Loss

games.title: Reserve rules
items: Reserves on admission are distributed among old partners in the new ratio.
They go in the old ratio.
If the workmen compensation claim exceeds the reserve, the excess is debited to the Revaluation Account.
It is a loss arising from reassessment of a liability.
Investment fluctuation reserve first absorbs any fall in the market value of investments.
Only the balance goes to old partners.
Advertisement suspense is credited to old partners' capitals.
It is a deferred expense, debited to old partners.
Reserves can be kept intact by a single adjusting entry.
The new partner is debited with his share and sacrificing partners credited.

quiz.q: General Reserve of ₹50,000 appears at the time of C's admission. A and B share 3:2. A's capital is credited with:
quiz.explain: Reserves belong to old partners in the old ratio: 50,000 × 3/5.
steps: Reserves belong to old partners in the old ratio 3:2.
Answer: ₹30,000
quiz.mistake: Includes the new partner or uses an equal split

quiz.q: Workmen Compensation Reserve ₹30,000; claim ₹20,000. Amount credited to old partners:
quiz.explain: The claim is provided for first; the excess ₹10,000 goes to old partners.
steps: WCR ₹30,000 first meets the claim of ₹20,000.
Excess = 30,000 − 20,000 = ₹10,000, credited to old partners.
Answer: ₹10,000
quiz.mistake: Distributes the whole reserve ignoring the claim

quiz.q: Workmen Compensation Reserve ₹30,000; claim ₹40,000. The extra ₹10,000 of claim is:
options: debited to the new partner's capital
quiz.explain: The reserve covers ₹30,000; the extra liability is a revaluation loss shared by old partners.
steps: The reserve of ₹30,000 covers only part of the ₹40,000 claim.
The extra ₹10,000 liability is a loss: debit the Revaluation Account.
Answer: debited to the Revaluation Account
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shortfall needs no entry

quiz.q: Advertisement Suspense of ₹12,000 appears in the balance sheet; A and B share 2:1. Amount debited to A:
quiz.explain: Deferred revenue expenditure is written off among old partners in the old ratio: 12,000 × 2/3.
steps: Advertisement Suspense is deferred revenue expenditure, written off in the old ratio 2:1.
Answer: ₹8,000
quiz.mistake: Credits it like a reserve or shares it equally

quiz.q: Investment Fluctuation Reserve ₹20,000; investments: book value ₹1,00,000, market value ₹92,000. Amount of the reserve credited to old partners:
quiz.explain: The fall of ₹8,000 is met from the reserve; the balance ₹12,000 goes to old partners.
steps: Fall = 1,00,000 − 92,000 = 8,000, met from the reserve
Balance of reserve = 20,000 − 8,000 = 12,000, credited to old partners
Answer: ₹12,000
quiz.mistake: Distributes the full reserve without adjusting the fall

quiz.q: Investment Fluctuation Reserve ₹20,000; investments: book value ₹1,00,000, market value ₹75,000. Amount debited to Revaluation Account:
quiz.explain: Fall ₹25,000; reserve absorbs ₹20,000; extra ₹5,000 is a revaluation loss.
steps: Reserve absorbs 20,000; extra = 25,000 − 20,000 = 5,000, debited to Revaluation A/c
Answer: ₹5,000
quiz.mistake: Debits the full fall to revaluation

quiz.q: Partners decide not to disturb a General Reserve of ₹60,000. C is admitted for 1/4 share. Amount debited to C's Capital in the adjusting entry:
quiz.explain: C would get 1/4 of the reserve in future, so he compensates sacrificing partners now: 60,000 × 1/4.
steps: C would later enjoy 1/4 of the undisturbed reserve.
So C compensates now: 60,000 × 1/4 = ₹15,000 debited to C's Capital.
Answer: ₹15,000
quiz.mistake: Charges C with the entire reserve

quiz.q: Why are accumulated reserves distributed among old partners in the old ratio on admission?
options: Because the new partner refuses them
Because reserves are liabilities to outsiders
They were earned when the old partners shared profits in that ratio
quiz.explain: Past profits belong to those who shared them, in the ratio then in force.
steps: Reserves were built from past profits shared in the old ratio.
So they are distributed among old partners in that ratio.
Answer: They were earned when the old partners shared profits in that ratio
quiz.mistake: Thinks the new partner has a right to past profits

teach.ask: Gappu's firm has a general reserve and some advertisement suspense when a new partner joins. Explain the treatment.
teach.praise: Well done! Reserves credited and fictitious losses debited to old partners, both in the old ratio.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: in which ratio, and to whom, does the general reserve go?

revise.summary: On admission, reserves and accumulated profits are credited, and accumulated losses and deferred revenue expenditure debited, to old partners in the old ratio. WCR and IFR first meet the claim or fall in value; any shortfall goes to the Revaluation Account.
focus: Workmen Compensation Reserve and Investment Fluctuation Reserve
remember: Reserves and P&L credit: Cr old partners (old ratio)
Losses, Advertisement Suspense: Dr old partners (old ratio)
Claim > WCR: excess debited to Revaluation A/c
traps: Don't give the new partner a share of past reserves
Credit only the excess of WCR over the claim
Undisturbed reserve: debit the new partner with his share

topics.title: Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities

learn.hook: That office in Gurugram bought years ago is worth much more now. Before a new partner joins, the old partners should pocket that gain.
points: Revaluation Account (a nominal account) records changes in asset and liability values on reconstitution.
Credit: increase in assets, decrease in liabilities, unrecorded assets. Debit: decrease in assets, increase in liabilities, unrecorded liabilities.
Balance: profit (credit side larger) or loss, transferred to OLD partners' capital accounts in the OLD ratio.
Entry for increase in asset: Dr Asset A/c, Cr Revaluation A/c. Decrease: Dr Revaluation A/c, Cr Asset A/c. Profit: Dr Revaluation A/c, Cr Old Partners' Capital A/cs.
After revaluation, prepare partners' capital accounts and the new balance sheet with revised values.

example.q: A and B (3:2) admit C. Building ₹2,00,000 is increased by 20%; stock ₹60,000 reduced by 10%; a 5% provision is made on debtors of ₹50,000; unrecorded investments ₹7,000; unrecorded outstanding salary ₹3,500; creditors reduced by ₹2,000. Find the revaluation result.
steps: Credits: building +40,000; investments 7,000; creditors 2,000 → ₹49,000.
Debits: stock 6,000; provision 2,500; outstanding salary 3,500 → ₹12,000.

learn.reallife: Land prices along new metro lines in Delhi, Bengaluru and Pune have jumped, so firms owning property there often show big revaluation gains when partners change.

games.title: Revaluation Account: debit or credit?
items: Increase in value of building
Unrecorded investment discovered
Decrease in creditors
Fall in value of stock
New provision for doubtful debts
Unrecorded outstanding expense
Depreciation on machinery

quiz.q: An increase in the value of an asset on revaluation is:
options: credited to the new partner's capital
debited to the asset's account and the old partners
quiz.explain: A rise in asset value is a gain, so the Revaluation Account is credited (and the asset debited).
steps: A rise in asset value is a gain.
Entry: Dr Asset A/c, Cr Revaluation A/c.
So it is credited to the Revaluation Account.
Answer: credited to the Revaluation Account
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the sides of the Revaluation Account

quiz.q: An unrecorded liability (e.g. outstanding salary) found on admission is:
options: debited to the old partners directly
quiz.explain: Recording a new liability is a loss to old partners, so Revaluation is debited.
steps: Recording a new liability is a loss to old partners.
So the Revaluation Account is debited.
Answer: debited to the Revaluation Account
quiz.mistake: Treats a new liability as a gain

quiz.q: Credits to Revaluation A/c total ₹49,000 and debits total ₹12,000. Result:
quiz.explain: Profit = credits − debits = ₹37,000.
steps: Revaluation profit = credits − debits.
Answer: ₹37,000
quiz.mistake: Adds both sides together

quiz.q: Revaluation profit of ₹37,000 is shared by A and B (3:2) before C's admission. A's share:
quiz.explain: Old partners share in the old ratio: 37,000 × 3/5.
steps: Old partners share revaluation profit in the old ratio 3:2.
Answer: ₹22,200
quiz.mistake: Includes the new partner or splits equally

quiz.q: Debtors ₹50,000 carry a provision of ₹1,000. A 5% provision is now required. Amount debited to Revaluation Account:
quiz.explain: Required ₹2,500 less existing ₹1,000 = extra ₹1,500.
steps: Answer: ₹1,500
quiz.mistake: Ignores the existing provision

quiz.q: Profit or loss on revaluation at the time of admission is shared by:
options: all partners in the new ratio
old partners in their old ratio
old partners in the sacrificing ratio
quiz.explain: The change in values arose before admission, so only old partners share it.
steps: Value changes arose before admission.
So old partners share revaluation profit or loss in the old ratio.
Answer: old partners in their old ratio
quiz.mistake: Uses the new ratio

quiz.q: The entry to transfer a revaluation LOSS is:
options: Dr Revaluation A/c / Cr Old Partners' Capital A/cs
Dr Profit and Loss A/c / Cr Revaluation A/c
Dr Old Partners' Capital A/cs / Cr Revaluation A/c
Dr New Partner's Capital A/c / Cr Revaluation A/c
quiz.explain: A loss reduces old partners' capitals, closing the Revaluation Account's debit balance.
steps: A loss reduces old partners' capitals and closes the Revaluation Account.
Entry: Dr Old Partners' Capital A/cs, Cr Revaluation A/c.
Answer: Dr Old Partners' Capital A/cs / Cr Revaluation A/c
quiz.mistake: Uses the profit entry for a loss

quiz.q: Machinery of ₹80,000 is depreciated by 10% and stock is appreciated by ₹5,000. Net result on revaluation (loss):
quiz.explain: Loss ₹8,000 on machinery, gain ₹5,000 on stock: net loss ₹3,000.
steps: Answer: ₹3,000
quiz.mistake: Adds the gain to the loss

quiz.q: Before C's admission, A's capital is ₹2,00,000. A is credited with ₹22,200 as his share of revaluation profit and ₹30,000 as his share of general reserve. A's capital shown in the new balance sheet (before any capital adjustment):
quiz.explain: All reconstitution gains are credited to A's capital account, and its closing balance goes to the new balance sheet: 2,00,000 + 22,200 + 30,000.
steps: Opening capital 2,00,000
Add revaluation profit 22,200 and reserve 30,000
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the reserve or the revaluation profit when preparing the capital account

teach.ask: Gappu must revalue his firm's assets before a new partner joins. Explain the Revaluation Account.
teach.praise: Excellent! Gains on the credit side, losses on the debit side, and the result goes to old partners in the old ratio.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: who gets the revaluation profit – and in which ratio?

revise.summary: The Revaluation Account records changes in values on reconstitution: credit for increases in assets, decreases in liabilities and unrecorded assets; debit for the opposite. Its profit or loss goes to old partners in the old ratio.
focus: What goes on each side of the Revaluation Account
remember: Credit: increase in assets, decrease in liabilities, unrecorded assets
Debit: decrease in assets, increase in liabilities, unrecorded liabilities
Profit or loss → old partners in old ratio
traps: The new partner does not share revaluation profit on admission
An unrecorded liability is a debit, not a credit
A revaluation loss is debited to capitals, not credited

topics.title: Adjustment of partners' capitals on admission

learn.hook: After all adjustments, do the partners' capitals match their profit shares? If not, someone tops up and someone withdraws.
points: Case 1 – new partner's capital from old partners' capitals: Total capital of new firm = Combined adjusted capitals of old partners ÷ their combined new share; New partner's capital = Total × his share.
Case 2 – old partners' capitals from new partner's capital: Total capital = New partner's capital ÷ his share; each old partner's required capital = Total × his new share.
Adjusted capital = capital after goodwill, reserves, revaluation and similar adjustments.
Excess capital is withdrawn (Dr Capital, Cr Cash) or transferred to current account; deficiency is brought in cash (Dr Cash, Cr Capital) or debited to current account.

example.q: C is admitted for 1/4 share and brings ₹60,000. New ratio A:B:C = 2:1:1. A's adjusted capital is ₹1,30,000 and B's ₹50,000. Adjust capitals.

learn.reallife: Like co-founders topping up their stake before a funding round, partners align capital with their new profit shares.

items.q: New partner brings ₹1,00,000 for 1/5. Total capital?
Old partners' capitals ₹3,00,000 for 3/4. New partner's capital for 1/4?

games.title: Capital adjustment facts
items: Capitals are adjusted on the basis of the new profit-sharing ratio.
Capitals are brought in line with new shares.
Excess capital may be transferred to the partner's current account.
Instead of paying cash, the excess can go to the current account.
Adjusted capital means capital before goodwill and revaluation adjustments.
It is after all such adjustments.
A partner with a deficiency of capital may bring cash to make it up.
Dr Cash, Cr his Capital A/c.
Total capital of the firm = new partner's capital × his share.
It is new partner's capital ÷ his share.

quiz.q: A's and B's adjusted capitals total ₹2,00,000 for their combined 4/5 share. C gets 1/5. C's capital should be:
steps: Answer: ₹50,000
quiz.mistake: Takes 1/5 of the old partners' capital instead of the new total

quiz.q: C brings ₹1,00,000 as capital for 1/5 share. Total capital of the new firm:
steps: Total capital = new partner's capital ÷ his share.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by the share instead of dividing

quiz.q: C brings ₹60,000 for 1/4 share. New ratio A:B:C = 2:1:1. A's required capital:
quiz.explain: Total capital ₹2,40,000; A's share 2/4 → ₹1,20,000.
quiz.mistake: Gives A the same capital as C

quiz.q: In the case above, A's adjusted capital is ₹1,30,000. A must:
quiz.explain: A has ₹10,000 more than required, so he withdraws the excess.
steps: From above: A's required capital = ₹2,40,000 × 2/4 = ₹1,20,000.
A's adjusted capital ₹1,30,000 − ₹1,20,000 = ₹10,000 excess.
So A withdraws ₹10,000.
Answer: withdraw ₹10,000
quiz.mistake: Reverses excess and deficiency

quiz.q: B's adjusted capital is ₹50,000 but his required capital is ₹60,000. B brings the deficiency in cash. The entry is:
options: Dr Cash A/c / Cr B's Capital A/c ₹10,000
Dr B's Capital A/c / Cr Cash A/c ₹10,000
Dr B's Current A/c / Cr B's Capital A/c ₹60,000
Dr Cash A/c / Cr Premium for Goodwill A/c ₹10,000
quiz.explain: Bringing cash increases both cash and B's capital.
steps: Deficiency = 60,000 − 50,000 = ₹10,000, brought in cash.
Cash increases and B's capital increases.
Entry: Dr Cash A/c, Cr B's Capital A/c ₹10,000.
Answer: Dr Cash A/c / Cr B's Capital A/c ₹10,000
quiz.mistake: Uses the withdrawal entry

quiz.q: Capitals are to be kept fixed. A partner's surplus capital after adjustment is:
quiz.explain: With fixed capitals, the surplus is credited to his current account.
steps: With fixed capitals, the capital account is not changed.
So the surplus is transferred to his current account.
Answer: transferred to his current account
quiz.mistake: Thinks surplus capital goes to reserves

quiz.q: Old partners' adjusted capitals: A ₹1,80,000 and B ₹1,20,000. D is admitted for 1/4 share. D's capital should be:
quiz.mistake: Takes 1/4 of the old capitals

quiz.q: 'Adjusted capital' of an old partner means capital after adjusting:
options: goodwill, reserves, revaluation and accumulated profits or losses
quiz.explain: Capitals are compared only after all reconstitution adjustments are made.
steps: Capitals are compared only after all reconstitution adjustments.
Adjusted capital = after goodwill, reserves, revaluation and accumulated profits or losses.
Answer: goodwill, reserves, revaluation and accumulated profits or losses
quiz.mistake: Uses opening capital before adjustments

teach.ask: Gappu has to make partners' capitals match the new ratio. Explain how.
teach.praise: Great! Find total capital, then each partner's required capital by new share, and settle the excess or shortage.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: how does he find the firm's total capital from the new partner's capital?

revise.summary: After all admission adjustments, capitals may be made proportionate to the new ratio. Total capital is found from the old partners' adjusted capitals or from the new partner's capital; excess is withdrawn or sent to current account, and deficiency is brought in or debited to current account.
focus: Finding the new partner's capital from old partners' capitals
Finding old partners' required capitals from the new partner's capital
remember: Total capital = new partner's capital ÷ his share
Required capital = total capital × new share
Excess: Dr Capital, Cr Cash (or Current A/c); deficiency: Dr Cash, Cr Capital
traps: Use adjusted capitals, not opening capitals
Divide by the share (1/5 → multiply by 5)
With fixed capitals, use current accounts for surplus or deficiency

topics.title: Change in profit-sharing ratio among existing partners

learn.hook: No one joins or leaves, yet the shares change – perhaps one partner now works harder. Whoever gains must pay the one who gives up.
points: On a change in ratio, some partners gain and some sacrifice: gain = new share − old share; sacrifice = old share − new share.
Goodwill: the gaining partner compensates the sacrificing partner for his share of goodwill – Dr Gaining Partner's Capital A/c, Cr Sacrificing Partner's Capital A/c.
Reserves and accumulated profits/losses are distributed in the OLD ratio (or adjusted by a single entry between gaining and sacrificing partners).
Revaluation profit or loss on a change in ratio is shared in the OLD ratio.

example.q: A and B share 3:2 and decide to share equally from now. Goodwill is valued at ₹1,00,000. Pass the goodwill entry.
steps: Dr B's Capital A/c 10,000 / Cr A's Capital A/c 10,000.
example.answer: Dr B's Capital A/c ₹10,000 / Cr A's Capital A/c ₹10,000

learn.reallife: When a partner in a family business starts handling the new Surat branch and gets a bigger share, the other partners are compensated for goodwill they give up.

games.title: Term ↔ meaning
pairs: Paid by gaining partner to sacrificing partner

games.title: Change in ratio checks
items: On a change in ratio, the gaining partner's capital is debited for goodwill.
He pays for the extra share.
Revaluation profit on a change in ratio is shared in the new ratio.
It belongs to the old arrangement, so the old ratio is used.
A partner whose share does not change neither pays nor receives goodwill.
He has neither gained nor sacrificed.
General reserve existing at the time of change is shared in the old ratio.
It was earned under the old ratio.
The sacrificing partner is debited with compensation for goodwill.
He is credited; the gaining partner is debited.

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2 and change to 1:1. Which statement is correct?
steps: So A sacrifices 1/10 and B gains 1/10.
Answer: A sacrifices 1/10 and B gains 1/10
quiz.mistake: Mixes up who gains and who sacrifices

quiz.q: A and B change their ratio from 3:2 to 1:1. Goodwill is ₹1,00,000. Compensation paid by B to A:
quiz.explain: Compensation = goodwill × gain = 1,00,000 × 1/10 = ₹10,000.
steps: Answer: ₹10,000
quiz.mistake: Uses the new share instead of the change in share

quiz.q: For the case above, the journal entry is:
options: Dr A's Capital A/c / Cr B's Capital A/c ₹10,000
Dr Goodwill A/c / Cr A's Capital A/c ₹10,000
Dr B's Capital A/c / Cr A's Capital A/c ₹10,000
Dr Cash A/c / Cr Goodwill A/c ₹10,000
quiz.explain: Gainer B is debited; sacrificer A is credited.
steps: Goodwill compensation = ₹1,00,000 × 1/10 = ₹10,000.
The gainer B pays the sacrificer A.
Entry: Dr B's Capital A/c, Cr A's Capital A/c ₹10,000.
Answer: Dr B's Capital A/c / Cr A's Capital A/c ₹10,000
quiz.mistake: Reverses the gaining and sacrificing partners

quiz.q: A, B and C share 3:2:1 and agree to share equally from now. Who neither gains nor sacrifices?
quiz.explain: B: 2/6 old and 2/6 new. A sacrifices 1/6; C gains 1/6.
steps: Old shares: A 3/6, B 2/6, C 1/6. New: 2/6 each.
A: −1/6 (sacrifice); C: +1/6 (gain); B: 2/6 → 2/6, no change.
So B neither gains nor sacrifices.
Answer: B
quiz.mistake: Assumes everyone's share changes

quiz.q: In the case above, goodwill is ₹60,000. Amount C pays to A:
quiz.explain: C gains 1/6 = A's sacrifice; 60,000 × 1/6 = ₹10,000.
steps: Answer: ₹10,000
quiz.mistake: Charges C for his full new share

quiz.q: A and B share 3:2 and change to 1:1. General Reserve of ₹30,000 is to be distributed. A gets:
quiz.explain: Reserves are distributed in the old ratio 3:2.
steps: On a change in ratio, reserves go in the old ratio 3:2.
Answer: ₹18,000
quiz.mistake: Uses the new equal ratio

quiz.q: A and B (3:2 → 1:1) prefer NOT to distribute a General Reserve of ₹50,000. In the single adjusting entry, B is debited by:
quiz.explain: B gains 1/10, so he compensates A for 1/10 of the reserve.
steps: Answer: ₹5,000
quiz.mistake: Debits B with his new share of the whole reserve

quiz.q: Revaluation profit arising on a change in profit-sharing ratio is shared in:
quiz.explain: The value change happened under the old arrangement.
steps: Value changes happened under the old arrangement.
So revaluation profit is shared in the old ratio.
Answer: the old ratio
quiz.mistake: Uses the new ratio

teach.ask: Gappu and his partner changed their ratio. Explain who pays whom for goodwill and how reserves are treated.
teach.praise: Spot on! The gainer compensates the sacrificer, and reserves and revaluation go in the old ratio.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: who is debited with goodwill when the ratio changes?

revise.summary: On a change in profit-sharing ratio, gaining partners compensate sacrificing partners for goodwill (Dr gainer, Cr sacrificer). Reserves, accumulated profits or losses and revaluation results are shared in the old ratio.
focus: Finding gain and sacrifice for each partner
Goodwill entry on a change in ratio
remember: Gain = new share − old share; sacrifice = old share − new share
Goodwill entry: Dr gaining partner, Cr sacrificing partner
Reserves and revaluation: old ratio
traps: Debit the gaining partner, not the sacrificing one
Don't distribute reserves in the new ratio
A partner with equal old and new shares neither gains nor sacrifices
